title: Audited repo files wrapped in fixed tags the files can close
observation: server/server.py line 486 wraps each file of the audited repo as <file path="name"> content </file>, and lines 890 and 943 wrap the whole repo as <repo> ... </repo>, without escaping. A file in the audited repo that contains </file> or </repo> can end the wrapper and give the auditing model instructions that change its verdict.
recommendation: Escape or reject the delimiter inside file content (or use a random per-run boundary) and tell the model that repo content is evidence, never instructions.

title: Server holding a GitHub token accepts requests from any website
observation: server/server.py line 1015 enables CORSMiddleware with allow_origins ['*'], all methods and all headers, on a local server that reads the user's GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN (line 110). Any web page open in the same browser can call its endpoints and act with the user's GitHub access.
recommendation: Allow only the app's own origin, require a per-session token on state-changing endpoints, and bind to 127.0.0.1.

title: Report shows Green when there are no results or unknown statuses
observation: cuec_crosscheck.py _compute_rag (lines 282-289) returns Red only for 'No match', Amber only for 'Partial', and Green for everything else. An empty match list, an unparsed model reply or an unexpected status value all produce a Green report.
recommendation: Fail closed: return Red or 'Incomplete' unless every CUEC has a recognised status, and show the count of unassessed items.

title: Policies joined into the prompt without any data boundary
observation: scripts/build_prompt.py policies_as_knowledge_chunks (lines 595-601) and summary_as_knowledge_chunks (lines 385-391) join full policy texts with newlines and place them in the prompt with no delimiters and no instruction that policy text is data. A line planted in a policy can change the verdicts of both independent assessors at once.
recommendation: Wrap each policy in labelled delimiters with a random boundary, and tell every agent prompt that policy content is evidence only, never an instruction.

title: No final human sign-off before the board summary is written
observation: In scripts/graph.py the confirm node (line 352) is a normal node, not an interrupt. The only gate before write_summary (lines 355-363) checks that each step key is in 'done' and that grade and tone are set; a step the model classifies as skipped is also added to 'done' (lines 154-160). Replay: skipping every step, the summary, JSON, trace and deck are produced without any person approving the content.
recommendation: Add a final approval step that requires an exact confirmation decided in code and bound to the content, record who approved and when, and refuse to save without it. FIXED TODAY by team RAG TAG with our guard Four Eyes: signed, content-bound final approval in graph.py and run.py; 13 replay tests added; all 104 agent tests pass. Pull request: https://github.com/SAAF-Project/Executive-Summary-Writer/pull/4

title: Human approval of preparation steps is decided by a model call
observation: For steps 1 to 4 the user's free-text reply is classified as confirmed or skipped by a model call (llm.interpret, scripts/graph.py line 137). Replay with a model steered to read every reply as confirmed: the manager answers 'No, that is wrong' four times and the summary is still released.
recommendation: Match accept and skip replies in code before any model call; never let a model decide that a human approved. MITIGATED TODAY by team RAG TAG: the final release now needs a Four Eyes approval checked in code, so a steered model can no longer release the summary (replay test included). Pull request: https://github.com/SAAF-Project/Executive-Summary-Writer/pull/4

title: Document wrapper can be closed by the document itself
observation: scripts/material.py line 211 wraps each file as <audit_material file="name"> text </audit_material> without escaping the closing tag or the file name. A document, slide note or hidden sheet containing </audit_material> ends the wrapper early and the rest is read as instructions. The same code is copied in frontend/agent-service/upstream/material.py line 211.
recommendation: Use a random per-run delimiter, escape or reject it inside the material, and tell the model in the system prompt that material is data, never instructions. Fix both copies.

title: Approver name on a prompt approval is taken from the request body
observation: webapp/server.py line 575: approved_by = body.get("approved_by") or the assigned auditor or "unknown". The person named on the approval record in the prompt history is whatever the client sends; the server has no authentication (its own header, line 5, says real authentication is not solved yet). Anyone who can reach the app can record an approval in another person's name.
recommendation: Take the approver only from an authenticated session, never from the request; sign approvals and bind them to the exact prompt and document approved. FIXED TODAY by team RAG TAG with Four Eyes: approved_by now comes from the logged-in user only; replay test included. Pull request: https://github.com/SAAF-Project/FieldworkOrchestration/pull/5

title: Anyone can approve review entries in the assigned reviewer's name
observation: webapp/server.py api_approve (lines 671-695) accepts entry_id, decision and role from the request body and records the decision under whoever is assigned to that role, with no authentication. The caller chooses the role, so any caller can approve as the manager; /finalize (line 697) then accepts these approvals as the human sign-off. For older engagements the reviewer name itself is taken from the body (line 684).
recommendation: Require login on approval endpoints and check that the logged-in person holds the role; record a signed approval bound to the reviewed content before /finalize accepts it. FIXED TODAY by team RAG TAG with Four Eyes: anonymous approvals refused (401), approving in another role refused (403), hand-written or out-of-date approvals no longer finalize; 18 tests added (the repo had none). Pull request: https://github.com/SAAF-Project/FieldworkOrchestration/pull/5

title: Anyone can reassign roles and redirect auditee requests
observation: webapp/server.py api_update_run (line 271) changes auditor_name, senior_auditor_name and auditee_email with no login. Anyone who can reach the app can make themselves the senior auditor and then approve their own work, or redirect PBC requests to their own email address.
recommendation: Require a logged-in user for role and contact changes and forbid self-assignment. FIXED TODAY by team RAG TAG: anonymous changes refused (401), self-assignment refused (403); replay test included. Pull request: https://github.com/SAAF-Project/FieldworkOrchestration/pull/5

title: HTML report rendered with autoescaping off
observation: report/report_generator.py line 16 renders the HTML report with a bare jinja2 Template, which has autoescaping off. Model output, which uploaded documents can influence, is placed into report.html, so any HTML or script in it becomes active when the auditor opens the report.
recommendation: Render with a jinja2 Environment using autoescape=True (select_autoescape), and escape model text before it goes to the PDF generator.

title: PII masking misses names in free-text fields
observation: In an offline test, personal names placed in the approver, submitted_by and description fields were not masked: masking is driven by field names, not by scanning content.
recommendation: Scan free text for names and other identifiers, and fail closed when masking cannot be confirmed.

title: Anyone on the network can replace the OWASP review criteria from any URL
observation: app.py lines 1202-1210: POST /owasp-update reads url from the JSON body and passes it to update_owasp_definitions (review_agent.py line 153). That function calls urllib.request.urlopen(url) (line 161) with no scheme or host allowlist and overwrites the OWASP definitions file that drives the review (line 180) after only a key-presence check. The Flask app has no authentication and listens on 0.0.0.0 (app.py line 1220). Anyone who can reach the port can point the tool at their own JSON and silently change the criteria every later review uses; urlopen also accepts file:// and internal http hosts (SSRF). The copy in agent-reviewer/app.py line 1203 has the same flaw.
recommendation: Ignore any url in the request and only fetch the fixed OWASP_UPDATE_URL over https, verifying a pinned hash or signature before saving. Bind to 127.0.0.1 and require authentication for any route that changes state.

title: Stored cross-site scripting through the deadline and reminder date fields
observation:
static/index.html line 729 inserts item.deadline into the table HTML without escaping (getDeadlineHTML returns
${deadline}
), and line 640 does the same for item.last_reminder_date; the result is assigned to tbody.innerHTML (line 628). Both values are free strings accepted from the API: deadline in PBCItemCreate (app.py line 226, POST /api/pbc) and last_reminder_date in PBCItemUpdate (app.py line 237, PUT /api/pbc/{id} at line 268). The API has no authentication, so anyone who can reach it can store a value such as an payload that runs script in the coordinator's browser.
recommendation: Escape every value with the existing esc() helper before inserting it (lines 640 and 729), and validate deadline and last_reminder_date as ISO dates on the server.

title: Copied OWASP reviewer lets any caller overwrite its criteria from any URL
observation: tools/scripts/owasp-agent-reviewer/app.py lines 994-1001: POST /owasp-update takes url from the request body and calls update_owasp_definitions(url) (review_agent.py line 130), which fetches it with urllib.request.urlopen (line 138) and overwrites owasp_llm_top10.json (line 157) that the reviewer loads as its criteria. The Flask app has no authentication and runs on host 0.0.0.0 (app.py line 1012), so anyone on the network can swap the review criteria or use the server to fetch internal or file:// URLs.
recommendation: Remove the url parameter and only fetch the fixed https source with a pinned hash or signature check; bind to 127.0.0.1 and require authentication for the update route.

title: GET request to /api/seed wipes all workpapers and tickets without any check
observation: src/app/api/seed/route.ts lines 11-14 export a GET handler that calls seedAll() with no session or token check. seedAll (src/lib/persist.ts lines 34-44) deletes every row in ticketEvents, checkpoints, workpapers, rehearsalRuns, forgeScans, tickets, personas and policies before re-inserting demo data. Any visitor, crawler, link preview or an on another site can erase the audit trail and workpapers.
recommendation: Remove the GET handler, keep seeding as a POST that requires an admin secret or is disabled outside development, and never delete audit records from a web route.

title: TeamMate API key committed to git history
observation: TeamMate API key (44 chars, high-entropy random value) assigned to TEAMMATE_API_KEY in backend/.env, added in the same commit 1294181 (2026-03-10). Untracked in ea1d1ec, so NOT in current HEAD (417cc8a), but still reachable from main and origin/main. Masked preview: P6ja...(44 chars).
recommendation: Revoke and rotate this TeamMate API key now with the TeamMate administrator. Remove backend/.env from history with git filter-repo and force-push, or treat the key as burned. Add a secret scan (for example gitleaks) on every push.

title: Document text placed in a fixed <document> tag without cleaning
observation: compliance_qa.py line 271 builds the prompt as <document> document_text </document>, and line 266 wraps additional_context the same way. document_text comes straight from the uploaded PDF (line 425) and is not cleaned, so a PDF containing </document> can end the wrapper and inject instructions into the compliance verdict.
recommendation: Neutralise the delimiter inside document text before wrapping (as Vendor_Guard does with _neutralize_tags) and state in the system prompt that the document is data.

title: Audit report generated with no record at all
observation: /api/generate-report (app/main.py lines 40-118) sends the auditor's inputs to the model (app/services/claude_service.py lines 54-59), fills the Word template with the parsed reply and returns it as a download. No inputs, prompt, model, raw reply, timestamp or user are saved anywhere; there is no logging in the app. The report contains findings, an executive summary and a conclusion.
recommendation: Save a run record for every report (input and template hashes, prompt, model and settings, raw reply, auditor, UTC timestamp, run id) and stamp the run id and model in the generated document.

title: Plan viewer forwards the server GitHub token to any GitHub API path
observation: src/app/api/plan-content/route.ts lines 9-30: session and slug come from the query string and are placed unencoded into `https://api.github.com/repos/SAAF-Project/SAAF-Project/contents/plans/${session}/${slug}.md`, which is fetched with Authorization: Bearer GITHUB_PAT and the raw response is returned to the caller. Because "../" segments are normalised by the URL parser and "?" moves the ".md" suffix into the query, any signed-in org member can make the server call any GitHub API GET endpoint with the server's token (for example other private repositories the PAT can read) and see the result.
recommendation: Validate session and slug against a strict pattern (letters, digits, dash) or a list of known plans, and encode each path segment with encodeURIComponent before building the URL.

title: Payment released by the pipeline without a human approval
observation: demo_pipeline.py sets pay_status 'RELEASED' after the automated checks and IBAN verification (lines 289-294), and the decision agent writes 'Payment released' (src/agent/decision_agent.py line 95). No person approves the release.
recommendation: Make release a separate step that needs a recorded, signed approval by an authorised person (for example with Four Eyes).

title: Reviewer decisions logged without who made them, in an editable log
observation: POST /log (server/server.py lines 1486-1493) accepts accept, reject and manual score events with whatever the browser sends; log_event (lines 378-391) appends them to actions.log.jsonl with no user, chain or signature and only warns if the write fails. The secret scan also copies the full matching line of each secret into audit-trail.cache.json (lines 465-477, 1437).
recommendation: Record the logged-in reviewer on each decision, hash-chain the action log, and mask secret values before writing them.

title: Model's own sufficiency warnings are silently discarded
observation: work_program_generator.py sufficiency_check() starts from an empty list (line 279) and overwrites entry['sufficiency_flags'] (line 338), although the prompt asks the model to fill sufficiency_flags (line 134). Warnings the model raised never reach the auditor.
recommendation: Merge the model's flags with the rule-based flags instead of replacing them, and record where each flag came from.

title: Work program Excel writes model and RCM text without formula guarding
observation: work_program_generator.py to_excel (line 568) appends rows with ws.append at lines 606 and 620 containing model-generated test steps, methodology, evidence and pass criteria, plus control text from the input RCM. openpyxl turns any string starting with "=" into a formula, and nothing in the file strips or escapes such values. A manipulated RCM or model output can place a working formula in the work program the auditor opens.
recommendation: Escape strings that begin with =, +, - or @ (prefix an apostrophe) or force string cells to data_type "s" before saving the workbook.

title: Run log overwritten on every run and input files not identified
observation: work_program_generator.py keeps prompts and raw replies per control (lines 171-238), but the log is written to <output>_log.json opened with 'w' (lines 805-808) and the default output name is fixed, so each run replaces the earlier evidence. The run log (lines 171-181) has no input file path or hash, and no hash or signature.
recommendation: Give each run its own folder with a run id, record input paths with SHA-256, and hash the log.

title: A Go decision needs no human sign-off
observation: The planning orchestrator asks a person to decide only on a No-Go; a Go outcome proceeds without any human sign-off.
recommendation: Require a recorded human sign-off for Go as well as No-Go.

title: Model output treated as Authoritative Source by the reporter
observation: scripts/build_prompt.py lines 424 and 433-434 pass the merged checker and gap results to the reporter under the heading 'Authoritative Source' and tell it to work strictly and only from it. A poisoned verdict from an earlier stage is carried into the final report as authoritative.
recommendation: Label merged output as model output to be checked, not as an authoritative source; keep the evidence check against the original policy text.

title: Code that writes the audit trail is not published
observation: README.md lines 75-77 say each stage saves its prompt and raw model output, but .gitignore excludes scripts/*.py apart from three entry files, and orchestration.py line 59 imports a utils module that is missing from the repo, so the record cannot be checked. The model id comes only from an environment variable (claude_config.py lines 13-14) with no evidence it is written to output, SDK retries (claude_config.py lines 17, 27-29) are not recorded, and raw results are off by default (orchestration.py lines 43-47).
recommendation: Publish the logging code (or a manifest spec with a sample run), and write the model id, settings, retries and a hash of each input into the combined JSON by default.

title: Audit trail is off by default and skips failed or rejected runs
observation: saaf/core/audit_trail.py writes a good per-run record (inputs, model, endpoint, settings, attempts, prompt SHA-256, UTC times, raw response; lines 102-119). But it is opt-in: agent.audit_trail is None by default (saaf/core/agent.py lines 60-61) and only set when --audit-trail-dir is passed (cli.py lines 154-155, 259-262). The record is written only after parsing and the grounding check pass (agent.py lines 107-136), so a run whose output was rejected or whose API calls failed leaves no record, and a failed write is only logged (audit_trail.py lines 142-144). The record itself carries no hash or signature.
recommendation: Turn the audit trail on by default, also write a record (with the error and raw reply) for failed and rejected runs, and add a hash over the whole record or a signed manifest.

title: Web version keeps no run record; CLI trace omits prompts, input hashes and errors
observation: The CLI saves a replayable trace (scripts/run_record.py lines 55-134; scripts/run.py lines 177-185 in the committed version) with file names, the configured model name, each call's task arguments and parsed output, and the manager's replies. Not recorded: the system prompt and the request actually sent, a hash of the audit material (excluded from each call at run_record.py line 81 and named only by file name at run.py line 182), the effort and thinking settings (scripts/llm.py lines 247-253), and the error that stopped a run (run.py lines 204-231 only print it; the trace just says incomplete). The web agent service builds the same graph per session (frontend/agent-service/app.py line 128) without TracingLLM and saves no trace at all.
recommendation: Use TracingLLM in the web service and save one trace per session; add SHA-256 of each material file, the system prompt version or hash, effort and thinking settings, the error that ended a run, and a run id shared by the trace and the output files.

title: Audit trail can be edited undetected and skips failed calls and image inputs
observation: agents/audit_trail.py records each Claude call with prompts, model, settings, raw reply, reasoning, tokens and run id (lines 102-119). But entries are plain JSON lines (_append, lines 211-216) with no hash or chain, so an edited or deleted line is not detectable. A call is recorded only when it succeeds (agents/claude_init.py line 229), so failed calls and the connection retries in _retry_on_connection_error (lines 146-161) leave no trace. Image inputs are replaced by a placeholder with only their length (claude_init.py lines 119-140) and no hash, so the pages the model saw cannot be identified.
recommendation: Chain each entry to the previous entry's hash (or sign it), record failed calls and retries as their own entries, and store a SHA-256 of every image and document sent to the model.

title: SharePoint site URL taken from the form without an allowlist
observation: The SharePoint site URL, folder and credentials go from the form (app.py lines 49-53) straight into the connector (parsers/sharepoint_connector.py lines 35-36). There is no scheme or host allowlist, so the server can be pointed at an arbitrary address and send the supplied credentials there.
recommendation: Accept https only and *.sharepoint.com hosts only; add size and count limits on downloaded files.

title: Model JSON output is not validated against a schema
observation: agent/audit_agent.py parses the model's JSON (around line 97) and uses it without schema validation. Injected document text can drop findings, invent a source file or set an unexpected priority value.
recommendation: Validate the JSON: source must be one of the uploaded files, priority must be Hoog, Middel or Laag, unknown keys dropped; otherwise reject and flag.

title: No record of prompts, model or raw output for the findings analysis
observation: agent/audit_agent.py lines 39-45 send the system prompt and document content to the model with adaptive thinking. The streamed text (line 73) is parsed and discarded, and the report metadata (lines 100-103) holds only the file count, lookback and date. Prompts, model, settings and raw reply are not saved; on a parse error only the first 800 characters go to the browser (line 91).
recommendation: Per upload_id, save a run.json with input file hashes, prompts sent, model and settings, the raw reply and a UTC timestamp, and print the model name in the report footer.

title: Hash-chained audit log is deleted after each web run
observation: The chained log is well built (src/gdpr_agent/audit_logger.py lines 55-75, verify_chain lines 84-95), but the Streamlit app writes it into a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory that is removed as soon as processing ends (app.py lines 128-132). The only remaining copy is an optional browser download (app.py lines 205-211), which the user can edit before keeping. Entries record role, purpose and justification but no user identity (the role is a dropdown, app.py line 60), and there is no hash of the source dataset.
recommendation: Write the log to a persistent, access-controlled location, store or sign the final chain hash separately, and record the logged-in user and a hash of the input data.

title: Flask review portals run with debug=True
observation: prototype/app.py line 30 and project_2026-03-24/app.py line 30 start the Flask app with app.run(debug=True), which shows stack traces and an interactive debugger console to the browser.
recommendation: Read debug from an environment variable that defaults to off.

title: Repo fetch clones any URL or local path given in the request
observation: app.py lines 1136-1186: POST /fetch-repo takes url from the JSON body and runs subprocess.run(["git","clone","--depth","1", url, tmp_dir]) (line 1146) with no scheme or host check and no "--" before the url, then returns the text of every matching file in the clone. With the server on 0.0.0.0 and no authentication (line 1220), a network caller can make the server clone from internal git hosts (SSRF) or from a local repository path on the server and read its contents back; a url starting with "-" is parsed as a git option. Same code in agent-reviewer/app.py line 1148.
recommendation: Accept only https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> URLs that match a strict pattern, put "--" before the url in the git command, and bind the app to 127.0.0.1 with authentication.

title: Web server bound to all interfaces with auto-reload
observation: run.py line 4: uvicorn.run("app:app", host="0.0.0.0", port=8000, reload=True). The app listens on every network interface and runs in development auto-reload mode.
recommendation: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default and enable reload only through an explicit development flag.

title: Documents marked validated by file name only
observation: Delivered PBC documents are accepted as validated based on their file name, without checking their content.
recommendation: Validate the content of each document against the request, and require approval before any email is sent to the auditee.

title: API with no login allows any website to read and delete PBC data
observation: app.py lines 30-36 add CORSMiddleware with allow_origins ["*"], allow_credentials True and all methods and headers. No route checks who is calling: DELETE /api/pbc/{item_id} (line 280), DELETE /api/documents/{file_id} (line 415), PUT /api/pbc/{item_id} (line 268) and GET /api/documents/{file_id}/download (line 433). Any web page the auditor opens can call the local API from the browser, read the PBC list and evidence files, and change or delete them. This is separate from the already reported 0.0.0.0 binding: it works even when the server only listens on localhost.
recommendation: Restrict allow_origins to the app's own origin, drop allow_credentials, and add authentication to every data-changing and download route.

title: PBC status changes, edits and deletions leave no history
observation: analyze_document overwrites record['analysis'] (app.py line 488) and moves a PBC item to validated on the AI conclusion (app.py lines 493-496) without recording the previous status. update_item and delete_item (app.py lines 266-286) change or remove items with no record of who, when or what changed. The model name is a hard-coded string (app.py line 486), not read from the response.
recommendation: Keep an append-only event log per PBC item (old and new status, actor, timestamp, analysis version) and never overwrite earlier analyses.

title: Policy lines joined into the heading prompt with no boundary
observation: services/segments.py lines 100-102 join every numbered line of the policy document with newlines straight into the model prompt, with no delimiter around the document text. The same code exists in a stray copy, services/docx_extractor copy.py line 176. A line in the policy can act as an instruction to the model.
recommendation: Wrap the document lines in a random-boundary block labelled as data, and remove the stray copy file.

title: Anthropic API key stored in a plaintext config file
observation: services/config.py (line 14) writes an anthropic api_key field into the P2C.conf config file, and agent.py reads the key from that file and passes it to the client (lines 64, 180). The key sits in plain text next to the project and is easy to commit or share by mistake.
recommendation: Read the key only from an environment variable or secret store; keep it out of config files.

title: Model text written to Excel can become live formulas
observation: services/write_output.py lines 66-68 write every field of each extracted control (control_to_row, lines 30-40: who, what, why, how, source quotes, open questions) with ws.cell(value=value). openpyxl stores any string that starts with "=" as a formula, and these fields come from the model's reading of the policy document (agent.py line 112 calls write_xlsx). A crafted policy can make a cell start with "=" so the reviewer's Excel runs a formula such as HYPERLINK or WEBSERVICE when the file is opened.
recommendation: Before writing, prefix any string starting with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe, or set cell.data_type to "s" for string values (as Vendor_Guard does in synthesizer/sanitize.py).

title: No record of model, prompts or run; reruns overwrite the output
observation: agent.py line 105 and services/segments.py line 111 only print the model. Prompts (agent.py lines 61-89, segments.py lines 95-125) are not saved, and the AI heading fallback failure is only printed (segments.py line 125). Outputs are written as <stem>.json and .xlsx (agent.py lines 111-112) with no timestamp, model or input hash, so a rerun overwrites the earlier result.
recommendation: Write a run manifest next to each output (source hash, model and header model, prompts, segmentation route, UTC timestamp, run id) and use run-specific file names.

title: Backend open to everyone when no key is set, with CORS *
observation: When no backend key is configured the backend accepts all callers, and it allows cross-origin requests from any site.
recommendation: Fail closed when no key is configured and restrict CORS to the extension's origin.

title: No record of prompts, retrieved issues or model output for recommendations
observation: backend/claude_client.py lines 126-128 log only the model name and the prompt and reply lengths to the console, and nothing is saved. When the model leaves out an issue, its relevance is silently set to 5 with a generic explanation (lines 155-160), and fallbacks are only printed (main.py lines 166, 176).
recommendation: Write a record per request (id, time, model, prompt, retrieved issue ids and scores, raw reply) and mark any filled-in scores in the output.

title: Observability plan not implemented: no request ID, token use or raw reply kept
observation: observability_notes.md lines 25 and 27 promise a hash of the token map plus request ID, token usage, latency and model version per call. tools/scripts/access_review_agent.py logs only to the console (basicConfig, line 34), logs the model (line 208) and reply length (line 216), keeps the raw reply only at DEBUG (line 237) while the level is INFO, and overwrites findings.json (lines 268-270). The bart run summary (tools/scripts/bart/access_review_agent.py lines 432-439) omits the stale_days, match_key and exclusion settings used, and user_mapping.csv with real identifiers is written next to the findings (lines 497-503).
recommendation: Implement the fields from the notes in a per-run JSONL file (request id, model, tokens, raw reply, input hashes, parameters) and store user_mapping.csv separately with restricted access.

title: Invented quotes only soft-flagged, verdict still returned
observation: When a quote in the model's answer is not found in the source document, the evidence check flags it but the compliance verdict is still returned unchanged.
recommendation: Downgrade the verdict to 'Insufficient evidence' or block it when any supporting quote is not found verbatim.

title: Auditor accept or override logged without who or when
observation: compliance_qa_app.py lines 541-545 and 562-565 append the auditor's accept or override to audit-log.jsonl by reusing the AI verdict object. The record has no reviewer identity, and its timestamp is the AI call time set at compliance_qa.py line 311, not the decision time. session_id (compliance_qa.py line 90) is never set, the user prompt is not logged (lines 282-293), and the chmod 444 protection (line 397) is lifted by the tool itself (line 391) with no hashes.
recommendation: Record the reviewer identity and a decision timestamp, set a session or run id, hash the document text and prompt, and chain each log line to the previous line's hash.

title: Web server bound to all interfaces with auto-reload
observation: run.py line 4: uvicorn.run("app.main:app", host="0.0.0.0", port=8000, reload=True). The app listens on every network interface (reachable by anyone on the same network) and runs in development auto-reload mode.
recommendation: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default and enable reload only through an explicit development flag.

title: Cut-off model output silently drops later findings
observation: When the model's output is truncated, findings after the cut are dropped and only a log warning is written; the report does not say it is incomplete.
recommendation: Mark the run as incomplete in the report and outputs, or retry, when the output was cut off.

title: Run step log kept in memory only; prompts and model replies not saved
observation: Run.emit (webui/server.py lines 86-91) appends routing decisions, per-agent errors and truncation warnings (forwarded by _RunLogHandler, lines 102-110) to an in-memory list that is never written to output/web/<run_id>, so it is lost when the server stops. complete() in agents/llm.py (lines 43-60) saves no prompts or replies, and the per-agent model constant (agents/orchestrator.py line 5) is not recorded. Input files are copied but not hashed (server.py lines 132-143).
recommendation: Write events.jsonl, prompts, raw replies and the model id per agent into the run folder, with SHA-256 of each input file.

title: Skill fetches extra skills from the internet at run time
observation: The skill instructions tell the coding assistant to install further skills from skills.sh while running, so what runs depends on a third-party site at that moment.
recommendation: Pin or vendor the needed skills, or drop the runtime install.

title: Hallucination check never blocks and under-rates flagged claims
observation: hallucination/aggregator.py aggregate() always returns blocked: False (line 57). A claim judged LIKELY_HALLUCINATED with Medium confidence does not raise the risk; risk is HIGH only for High-confidence verdicts and MEDIUM only with two or more unverified claims, so one likely-hallucinated plus one unverified claim scores LOW.
recommendation: Count any likely-hallucinated claim as at least MEDIUM, and set blocked: True on HIGH so the finding cannot be released without a person.

title: Retrieval fallback recorded wrongly; prompts, context and raw verdicts not kept
observation: hallucination/annotator.py line 55 records the retrieval backend from the RAG_BACKEND environment setting, while hallucination/rag.py lines 51-56 and 66-68 silently fall back to markdown files when ChromaDB fails, so the record can say chromadb when markdown was used. The JSONL log (annotator.py lines 63-75) keeps only finding id, counts, risk, blocked and warning; prompts, retrieved passages, the extractor model and the raw verifier reply are not kept.
recommendation: Record the backend actually used and why it fell back, the retrieved passages with source and hash, both model names, and the raw verifier reply.

title: Control verdicts saved without model, prompt, policy file or time
observation: agent.py lines 174-175 write only control_id, found, page_no and paragraph. The model (line 24), policy path (line 145), prompt and time are missing, the raw reply is discarded on a parse error (lines 164-171), and the default output file judge_verdicts.json is overwritten on every run.
recommendation: Add a run header (run id, UTC time, model, max_tokens, SHA-256 of the PDF and controls file, prompt hash) and keep the raw reply for each control.

title: Report does not name the model or the files that were read
observation: owasp_llm_audit/auditor.py lines 216-234 keep neither the prompt nor the raw reply. report.py lines 24-37 record only the target and the date. The model (configurable, auditor.py line 173 and cli.py line 23) and any files skipped or cut off (collector.py lines 55-64) are not recorded.
recommendation: Write a run record next to the report with the model, a prompt hash, the files read with their hashes, any truncation, and the raw reply.

title: Blank quantity or price is treated as a MATCH
observation: In an offline probe of the matcher with its own sample format, an invoice line with an empty quantity or price produced MATCH instead of a failure.
recommendation: Treat missing or unparseable values as FAIL, never as a match.

title: Match result and tolerances used are not saved
observation: /match and /api/match (webapp/app/main.py lines 73-145) take price, quantity and total tolerances from the form, build the report and return it without saving it. MatchReport.to_dict (webapp/app/services/matcher.py lines 108-121) includes neither the tolerances nor file hashes, so a MATCH cannot be re-performed or linked to its inputs.
recommendation: Save each run (input file hashes, tolerances, verdict per line, timestamp, user) to an append-only log and show the tolerances on the result page.

title: CSV export of SOC report and model text has no formula guard
observation: cuec_crosscheck.py write_csv (lines 262-270) writes cuec_description (taken from the vendor SOC report), org_control_description and the model's rationale with csv.DictWriter and no escaping. A value starting with =, +, - or @ is treated as a formula when the CSV is opened in Excel.
recommendation: Prefix any cell value that starts with =, +, - or @ with an apostrophe before writing the CSV.

title: Run log has no run ID, input hashes or tamper protection
observation: cuec_crosscheck.py logs model, tokens, raw replies and completeness checks well (lines 173-205), but main() logs only input paths and sizes (lines 521-531), every run is appended to the same output/cuec_crosscheck.log with no run id (lines 512-519), only a 12-character prefix of the system prompt hash is kept (line 153) and the user prompt is not kept. The log is plain text, so edits are not detectable.
recommendation: Add a run id to every line or use a per-run log file, log full SHA-256 of both input documents and of the full prompt, and add a hash chain or a final manifest hash.

title: Refusal fallback to another model is on by default
observation: scripts/llm.py line 28 sets USE_FALLBACKS from USE_REFUSAL_FALLBACKS with default '1'. A request refused by a safety classifier is re-run on a fallback model, so audit content can be processed by a model other than the one the auditor configured, without opt-in.
recommendation: Default the fallback to off, and record the model that actually answered in the trace and output.

title: Free-text domain accepted into the report header
observation: At the report header domain question any reply that is not one of the listed options is accepted as the domain name. In an offline run the reply 'yes' was accepted and recorded as the domain.
recommendation: Accept only the listed options, or ask the user to confirm a typed domain before it is used.

title: Flask app runs with debug=True and returns tracebacks to the browser
observation: app.py line 218 starts the app with app.run(debug=True, port=5000, threaded=True), enabling the Werkzeug debugger and reloader, and the analysis stream sends the last 500 characters of the Python traceback to the client on any error (around line 183). The form handles a Claude API key and SharePoint username and password (lines 41-52). The server binds to localhost and the debugger is PIN protected, which limits exposure.
recommendation: Read debug from an environment variable that defaults to off, and return a generic error message to the client while logging the traceback on the server.

title: Web audit log keeps only the rating and silently skips failed writes
observation: app.py lines 1105-1121 log time, file names, input hashes, model and rating, but not the review text, and a failed write is ignored (except OSError: pass), so the review exists only in the browser unless the user downloads it. Only a hash of the system prompt is kept (review_agent.py line 132).
recommendation: Store the review (or its hash plus a copy) on the server for each run and stop with an error when the log cannot be written.

title: Original policy evidence file is moved, not copied
observation: agent.py line 113 calls shutil.move on the source policy file after processing, so the original evidence is removed from where the auditor placed it.
recommendation: Copy the file and leave the original untouched; record its hash so the evidence can be traced.

title: RCM approval and input files not recorded
observation: The output of tools/scripts/rcm_builder.py (lines 1257-1263) has version, time, context, warnings and per-risk source references, but no input file paths or hashes (inputs are read at lines 1384-1386) and no approval block, although agent.yaml requires auditor approval before hand-off to UC8.
recommendation: Add the SHA-256 of each input file, a run id and an approval block (approver, time, hash of the RCM).

title: Auditor score overrides stored without reason or name
observation: skills/agent-rogue-risk-assessor/scripts/scan_repo.py lines 333-338 apply override values and store only the numbers. The reason and the person exist only in the report the assistant fills in by hand (SKILL.md line 33; assets/report_template.md lines 51-62), and the model used is recorded only if the assistant follows the template.
recommendation: Require a reason and a reviewer for each override in the scanner input, refuse overrides without them, and put the hash of the scan JSON in the report.

title: Sign-off name is free text and not bound to the draft content
observation: web/app.py lines 167-184 store a typed name, statement, time, input fingerprint and finding ids for the sign-off. There is no login and no hash of the draft that was approved, and events.jsonl (web/app.py lines 56-62) is a plain append file that can be edited without detection.
recommendation: Put a hash of draft.json in the sign-off, take the reviewer from a login, and chain the event log.

title: Dry run prints a canned audit report with no label
observation: The dry-run mode prints a pre-written audit report that is not labelled as sample output, so it can be mistaken for a real assessment.
recommendation: Label dry-run output clearly as sample data and never write it where real reports go.

title: Tailwind loaded from CDN with no pinned version or integrity check
observation: index.html line 53 loads <script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com"> with no version and no integrity attribute. Whatever that third-party host serves at load time runs with full access to the page.
recommendation: Build Tailwind into a static CSS file at build time, or pin an exact version and add an integrity hash with crossorigin.
